Past simple: played, went, saw.explain_en: We use the past simple for actions that started and finished in the past. We often say when: yesterday, last week, in 2020, two days ago.
Past simple: played, went, saw.explain_ar: بنستخدم الماضي البسيط لحاجات حصلت وخلصت في الماضي، وغالباً بنقول إمتى: yesterday وlast week وtwo days ago.

examples.en: We moved here two years ago.

check.question: Which sentence is past simple?
options: I watched a film last night.
check.why_ar: last night زمن خلص، والفعل watched ماضي.

Past simple: played, went, saw.explain_en: Regular verbs add -ed: play → played, study → studied. Irregular verbs change: go → went, see → saw, eat → ate, have → had. The verb is the same for everyone.
Past simple: played, went, saw.explain_ar: الأفعال المنتظمة بتاخد ed: played وstudied. والشاذة بتتغير: went وsaw وate وhad. والفعل واحد مع كل الضمائر.
Past simple: played, went, saw.board: play → played · go → went · see → saw

check.question: Last summer we ___ to Alexandria.
check.why_ar: go فعل شاذ وماضيه went.

Past simple: played, went, saw.explain_en: To say no, use “didn’t” and the base verb: “I didn’t go”, not “I didn’t went”. Arabic speakers often put the past form twice — remember: only one past!
Past simple: played, went, saw.explain_ar: للنفي: didn’t + الفعل في أصله: “I didn’t go” مش “I didn’t went”. خلي بالك: الماضي مرة واحدة بس.

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
check.why_ar: بعد didn’t الفعل بيرجع لأصله: come.

Past simple: played, went, saw.explain_en: Questions use “Did … + base verb?”: “Did you enjoy the trip?”. Use the past simple to tell what happened in order: first, then, after that.
Past simple: played, went, saw.explain_ar: السؤال: Did + الفعل في أصله: “Did you enjoy the trip?”. وبنحكي اللي حصل بالترتيب بـ first وthen وafter that.
Past simple: played, went, saw.board: Did you …? → Yes, I did. / No, I didn’t.

examples.en: Did you have fun? — Yes, I did!
First we ate, then we played football.

check.question: “___ you finish your homework?” — “Yes, I did.”
check.why_ar: سؤال عن الماضي بأفعال عادية بيبدأ بـ Did.

Past simple: played, went, saw.recap_en: The past simple is for finished actions. Regular verbs add -ed, irregular verbs change, and we use didn’t and did with the base verb.

Present continuous: I am playing.explain_en: We use the present continuous for actions happening now, at this moment: “I am reading”, “Look! It’s raining.”
Present continuous: I am playing.explain_ar: بنستخدم المضارع المستمر لحاجة بتحصل دلوقتي حالاً: “I am reading”.
Present continuous: I am playing.board: now · at the moment · Look! · Listen!

examples.en: She is talking on the phone.

check.question: Which sentence is happening now?
check.why_ar: now بتدل على حاجة بتحصل دلوقتي.

Present continuous: I am playing.explain_en: Make it with am, is or are and the verb + -ing. Spelling: write → writing (drop e), swim → swimming (double the letter).
Present continuous: I am playing.explain_ar: بنكوّنه بـ am أو is أو are + الفعل + ing. انتبه: writing (شيل e)، وswimming (كرر الحرف).

examples.en: We are waiting for the bus.

check.question: Look! The children ___ in the pool.
check.why_ar: are + swimming (بنكرر m).

Present continuous: I am playing.explain_en: A common mistake is “I playing” without am. In English we need both parts: “I am playing.” Also, verbs like like, know and want don’t usually take -ing.
Present continuous: I am playing.explain_ar: غلطة مشهورة: “I playing” من غير am. لازم الجزئين: “I am playing.” وأفعال زي like وknow وwant غالباً ما بتاخدش ing.

examples.en: I know the answer. (not I am knowing)

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
check.why_ar: لازم is + cooking.

Present continuous: I am playing.explain_en: Ask with am, is or are first: “Are you coming?”. We also use it for fixed plans soon: “I’m meeting Sara tomorrow.”
Present continuous: I am playing.explain_ar: بنسأل بـ am أو is أو are في الأول: “Are you coming?”. وبنستخدمه كمان لمواعيد قريبة متفق عليها: “I’m meeting Sara tomorrow.”

examples.en: What are you doing? — I’m cooking.
We’re flying to Dubai on Monday.

check.question: “What ___ you doing now?”
check.why_ar: السؤال بالمستمر مع you بيبدأ بـ are.

Present continuous: I am playing.recap_en: Use am, is or are with verb-ing for actions happening now and for near plans. Never forget the “be” part.

Comparing: bigger / more beautiful.explain_en: To compare two things, short adjectives add -er and we use “than”: tall → taller than, cheap → cheaper than. Big doubles the letter: bigger.
Comparing: bigger / more beautiful.explain_ar: عشان نقارن حاجتين، الصفة القصيرة بتاخد er وبعدها than: taller than. وbig بتبقى bigger.
Comparing: bigger / more beautiful.board: tall → taller than · big → bigger than

examples.en: My brother is taller than me.
This bag is cheaper than that one.

check.question: Riyadh is ___ than Abha in summer.
check.why_ar: hot صفة قصيرة: hotter، وبنكرر t.

Comparing: bigger / more beautiful.explain_en: Long adjectives use “more”: beautiful → more beautiful, expensive → more expensive. Words ending in -y change to -ier: easy → easier, happy → happier.
Comparing: bigger / more beautiful.explain_ar: الصفات الطويلة بنستخدم معاها more: more beautiful. واللي آخرها y بتبقى ier: easier.

examples.en: English is easier than I thought.

check.question: Which is correct?
check.why_ar: interesting صفة طويلة، فبنستخدم more.

Comparing: bigger / more beautiful.explain_en: Some are irregular: good → better, bad → worse, far → farther. Never use “more” and “-er” together: say “bigger”, not “more bigger”.
Comparing: bigger / more beautiful.explain_ar: فيه صفات شاذة: better وworse وfarther. وماينفعش نجمع more مع er: “more bigger” غلط.

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
check.why_ar: good في المقارنة بتبقى better لوحدها.

Comparing: bigger / more beautiful.explain_en: To compare with everyone, use “the … -est” or “the most …”: the tallest, the most beautiful, the best. “He is the best player in the team.”
Comparing: bigger / more beautiful.explain_ar: عشان نقارن بالكل: the + est أو the most: the tallest وthe most beautiful وthe best.
Comparing: bigger / more beautiful.board: the tallest · the most beautiful · the best

examples.en: It’s the biggest city in Egypt.

check.question: Everest is ___ mountain in the world.
check.why_ar: مقارنة بالكل لصفة قصيرة: the highest.

Comparing: bigger / more beautiful.recap_en: Short adjectives add -er and -est, long ones use more and the most, and good and bad become better, worse, the best and the worst.

much / many / a lot of.explain_en: Some things we can count: one apple, two apples. Others we can’t: water, money, time, rice. This changes the words we use for quantity.
much / many / a lot of.explain_ar: فيه حاجات بنعدها: apple وapples. وحاجات ما بتتعدش: water وmoney وtime وrice. وده بيغير الكلمات اللي بنستخدمها للكمية.
much / many / a lot of.board: countable: apples, books · uncountable: water, money

check.question: Which word is uncountable?
check.why_ar: rice ما بيتعدش (مش بنقول two rices).

much / many / a lot of.explain_en: Use “many” with countable plurals (many friends) and “much” with uncountable things (much time). We mostly use them in questions and negatives.
much / many / a lot of.explain_ar: many مع الجمع اللي بيتعد (many friends)، وmuch مع اللي ما بيتعدش (much time). وأكتر استخدامهم في الأسئلة والنفي.

examples.en: How many brothers do you have?

check.question: How ___ sugar do you want?
check.why_ar: sugar ما بيتعدش، فبنستخدم much.

much / many / a lot of.explain_en: In positive sentences we usually say “a lot of” — it works with both kinds: a lot of friends, a lot of time. It sounds more natural than much in everyday English.
much / many / a lot of.explain_ar: في الجمل المثبتة غالباً بنقول a lot of، وبتنفع مع النوعين: a lot of friends وa lot of time. وهي أطبع من much في الكلام.

examples.en: She has a lot of books.
We had a lot of fun.

check.question: Most natural: “There is ___ traffic today.”
check.why_ar: traffic ما بيتعدش، وفي الجملة المثبتة a lot of هي الأطبع.

much / many / a lot of.explain_en: Use “some” in positive sentences and “any” in questions and negatives. “A few” = a small number (a few friends), “a little” = a small amount (a little milk).
much / many / a lot of.explain_ar: some في المثبت، وany في الأسئلة والنفي. a few = عدد قليل (a few friends)، وa little = كمية قليلة (a little milk).
much / many / a lot of.board: a few + count · a little + no count

check.question: I invited ___ friends to my party.
check.why_ar: friends بيتعدوا، فبنقول a few.

much / many / a lot of.recap_en: Use many with things we count and much with things we can’t, mostly in questions and negatives. A lot of works with both in positive sentences.

Going to: future plans.explain_en: We use “going to” to talk about plans we have already decided: “I’m going to study medicine.”
Going to: future plans.explain_ar: بنستخدم going to لخطط قررناها خلاص: “I’m going to study medicine.”

examples.en: We’re going to visit Cairo next month.
examples.ar: إحنا ناويين نزور القاهرة الشهر الجاي.

examples.en: She’s going to learn to drive.

check.question: Which sentence is a plan?
options: I’m going to buy a new phone.
check.why_ar: going to بتعبر عن خطة في المستقبل.

Going to: future plans.explain_en: Use am, is or are + going to + the base verb: “He is going to play.” Don’t forget the verb “be”.
Going to: future plans.explain_ar: am أو is أو are + going to + الفعل في أصله: “He is going to play.” وماتنساش be.
Going to: future plans.board: am / is / are + going to + verb

examples.en: I’m going to call my mum.
They are going to watch the match.

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
check.why_ar: لازم is، والفعل بعد to في أصله.

Going to: future plans.explain_en: We also use going to when we can see something will happen: “Look at those clouds — it’s going to rain!”
Going to: future plans.explain_ar: وبنستخدمه كمان لما نشوف دليل إن حاجة هتحصل: “Look at those clouds — it’s going to rain!”
Going to: future plans.board: I can see it → going to

examples.en: Be careful! You’re going to fall!
The team is winning. They’re going to win the cup.

check.question: The sky is dark. It ___ rain.
check.why_ar: شايفين دليل (السما مضلمة)، فـ is going to.

Going to: future plans.explain_en: Ask: “Are you going to come?” Say no: “I’m not going to stay.” In fast speech, people often say “gonna” — but write “going to”.
Going to: future plans.explain_ar: السؤال: “Are you going to come?” والنفي: “I’m not going to stay.” وفي الكلام السريع بيقولوا gonna، لكن في الكتابة going to.
Going to: future plans.board: Are you going to …? · I’m not going to …

examples.en: What are you going to do this weekend?
He isn’t going to come today.

check.question: “___ you going to watch the film?”
check.why_ar: السؤال بـ be: Are you going to …?

Going to: future plans.recap_en: Use am, is or are + going to + verb for plans you have decided and for things you can see will happen.

in / on / at for time.explain_en: Use “at” for exact times and some short expressions: at 7 o’clock, at noon, at night, at the weekend (British English).
in / on / at for time.explain_ar: at مع الساعة بالظبط وتعبيرات زي at noon وat night.

check.question: The film starts ___ 8 o’clock.
check.why_ar: مع الساعة بالظبط بنستخدم at.

in / on / at for time.explain_en: Use “on” for days and dates: on Monday, on Friday morning, on 15 May, on my birthday.
in / on / at for time.explain_ar: on مع الأيام والتواريخ: on Monday وon 15 May وon my birthday.
in / on / at for time.board: on Monday · on 3 March · on my birthday

check.question: My birthday party is ___ Saturday.
check.why_ar: مع الأيام بنستخدم on.

in / on / at for time.explain_en: Use “in” for months, years, seasons and parts of the day: in July, in 2025, in summer, in the morning. But we say “at night”!
in / on / at for time.explain_ar: in مع الشهور والسنين والفصول وأجزاء اليوم: in July وin summer وin the morning. لكن بنقول at night!
in / on / at for time.board: in May · in 2026 · in the morning

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: I go to school in Sunday.
I go to school in the morning.
I go to school at the morning.
check.why_ar: أجزاء اليوم بـ in: in the morning.

in / on / at for time.explain_en: We don’t use in, on or at with today, tomorrow, yesterday, next and last: “See you tomorrow”, “I met him last week” — not “on last week”.
in / on / at for time.explain_ar: مش بنستخدم in أو on أو at مع today وtomorrow وyesterday وnext وlast: “I met him last week”.
in / on / at for time.board: next week · last Friday · tomorrow (no preposition)

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
check.why_ar: مع next مفيش حرف جر.

in / on / at for time.recap_en: Use at for clock times, on for days and dates, and in for months, years, seasons and parts of the day. Use nothing before next, last, today and tomorrow.
